Echoed literal: no. The expected groups 0/4/0 and their hosts are literals from the module-level comment, computed outside the helper. The mod-3 values were observed in probe output `GROUPS3 {'a.example': 2, 'c.example': 2, 'f.example': 0, 'h.example': 0, 'j.example': 1, 'k.example': 0}`. The test does not perform the group computation itself. Production lines whose deletion turns it red: the pointer write call to be placed after the merge `run_cmd` (updater-worker.py:1476-1488) and before the popularity `run_cmd` (1500). Today it does not exist, and 155/157 are red.\n\n4. One value: yes before the rewrite. `increments` was read only at N 7, which could not tell \"writes args.increments\" from a constant 7. In the N-7-prior case it also could not tell it from \"copies the prior pointer's N\". The added `n3-over-n7-pointer-crawls-0` case reads both `increments` (expects 3) and `last_group` (expects 0, the N-changed restart) at a second N. `last_group` is now read at three inputs.\n\n5. The double: no. Only `subprocess.run` (the severed child-process layer) and `run_similarity_stage` (a recorder past the measured window) are replaced. `main`, `single_run_lock`, `read_increment_pointer`, the staging filter, and real schema.sql prod/staging all run for real.\n\n6. It collects: yes. The run printed `collected 6 items` (3 success + 3 stop cases), which matches what I wrote. `_run_increment_main` gained an `increments` keyword, and every caller passes names that exist.\n\n7. Observed, not predicted: yes, every expectation was observed. The probe `tests/tmp/probe_63_phase2_rewrite.py` printed:\n- `N3 None [['f.example', 'h.example', 'k.example']] [b'{\"last_group\": 3, ...}\\n'] ... 1`: the N-3 run completes, crawls f/h/k (group 0), and reaches similarity once.\n- `LOCK 1170809 RuntimeError Another updater run is active (pid=1170809); lock exists at ... [] True`: the live-pid lock refuses with that message, runs no child, and leaves the pointer intact.\nThe fail-before-merge and merge-child-fails control values were already observed by the earlier `probe_63_phase2_harness.py`, and the run below confirms them. I have no delete tool, so `tests/tmp/probe_63_phase2_rewrite.py` is still on disk; the real test now carries what it showed and it can be removed.\n\n8. Red, not green: yes. ValidateTests on the rewritten file: `3 failed, 3 passed`, `[exit status 1]`. All three C1 success cases fail. The three C2 cases pass. That is inherent to a preservation clause against code that never writes the pointer. What makes C2 measure something is that the same file proves the write exists once the phase lands (155/157), and C2's controls pin where each run stopped.\n\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. Every control passed in all three failures (151-153, and 154 at the merge child), so the run reached the judging assertions:\n- n7-no-pointer-crawls-0 failed at line 155: `assert (1 == 1 and None is not None)`. The popularity child ran once and the pointer file did not exist.\n- n7-last-3-crawls-4 failed at line 157: `AssertionError: {'last_group': 3, 'increments': 7, 'completed_at': '2026-10-01T20:00:00Z'}`, `assert 3 == 4`.\n- n3-over-n7-pointer-crawls-0 failed at line 157: `assert 3 == 0`, with the same unchanged prior pointer.\nThat is exactly \"the phase's pointer write is not implemented\". No import, typo, path or harness failure.\n\n10. Observed expected output: yes. Row 154's `[None]`/`[PRIOR_POINTER]` passed in the run. Rows 155/157 failed showing the current values (`[None]`; last_group 3), and their expected values (non-None; 0/4/0) come from the observed channels-child hosts at line 153, which passed in all three cases. Row 183's `PRIOR_POINTER` passed in all three stop cases (`3 passed`). The run contradicted none of the expected values.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:2": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py`\n- Added `write_increment_pointer(state_path, group, increments)` after `read_increment_pointer`. It writes `{\"last_group\": group, \"increments\": increments, \"completed_at\": \"<UTC ISO-8601 Z>\"}\\n`, the same shape `read_increment_pointer` reads back. The write is atomic: `tempfile.mkstemp` in the pointer's own directory (named `<pointer name>.<random>.tmp`), write, `fsync`, then `os.replace` over the pointer. If anything fails, the temp file is removed and the error re-raised. A crash therefore leaves either the old pointer or the new one, never a half-written file. It logs `increment written last_group=\u2026 n=\u2026 state=\u2026`.\n- In `main()`, with `--increments >= 1`, `write_increment_pointer(increment_state, selected_group, args.increments)` is called right after the `merge-staging-db.py` `run_cmd` returns, before the denylist safety prune and the `recompute-popularity.py` child (C1). A run that stops earlier never reaches it, so the pointer stays byte-identical (C2). That covers `--fail-before-merge`, a merge child exiting non-zero (`run_cmd` raises `CalledProcessError`), and a held run lock. A failure in a later step leaves the pointer advanced, so a group that is already merged is not crawled again.\n\n### `.gitignore`\n- Added `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json*`. This ignores the default pointer file (`updater-increment.json` next to the default prod DB in `engine/server/db/`) and any temp file a crashed write leaves behind. Neither is matched by the existing `*.db*` patterns.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

The same test then makes an unlocked `--fail-before-merge` run through the new `_run_armed` helper, and :204 asserts exactly one `increment read` record across both runs. That is the positive control: a run that reads the pointer logs the record, so finding none for the refused run means it never read. This rules out an implementation that reads the pointer before taking the lock. I checked that with a probe variant, `read-early`, which moves the read-and-log block above `with single_run_lock(lock_file):`.     "step_7_implement:3": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py`\n\n`main()` now logs `increment pointer not advanced` for every `--increments` run that read the pointer and did not advance it, and holds a failed pointer write until the global post-merge steps have run.\n\n- **New `pointer_pending` flag.** It is set to True right after `read_increment_pointer` succeeds. It goes back to False once `write_increment_pointer` has returned or has logged its own failure.\n- **New `except BaseException` clause** on the outer `try` around `single_run_lock` (it re-raises). When `pointer_pending` is still True, it logs `increment pointer not advanced group=<g> state=<path>: <exc>`. This covers C1:\n  - a run stopped by `--fail-before-merge` or by the merge child failing gets exactly one line carrying that error's text;\n  - a run refused at the lock never read the pointer, so it logs nothing;\n  - a completed run already cleared the flag, so it logs nothing.\n- **Pointer write failure (C2).** The `write_increment_pointer` call after the merge is now wrapped in `except OSError`. On failure it logs one `increment pointer not advanced ... ; running post-merge steps before failing the run` line, keeps the error in `pointer_error` and lets the run continue: denylist prune, popularity, ANN build, Engine start, crawl.db copy, trending and the similarity stage.\n- **End of the run.** After `run_similarity_stage`, a held `pointer_error` raises `RuntimeError(\"increment pointer not advanced: <error>\")`, chained from the original error. So the run fails and never logs `worker completed`. The flag is already False by then, so the outer handler does not log a second line.\n- **When both fail.** This check comes before the existing trending-error raise. If the pointer write and trending both fail, the pointer error is what gets raised; the trending failure is still logged as before.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

    "step_9_triage": "<docs>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe doc describes a full crawl on a weekly timer. Each part below is now wrong or missing.\n\n- **Purpose / Inputs and Outputs (5-36).**\n  - Add the per-run host group.\n  - Add the pointer file `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json` (next to the resolved `--prod-db`, overridable with `--increment-state`). Its content is `{\"last_group\", \"increments\", \"completed_at\"}`, and a crashed write leaves a `updater-increment.json.<random>.tmp` temp file. Both are gitignored.\n  - Line 186 says staging is \"recreated each run\". It is now also filtered to the group.\n- **Execution Order (42-89).** Add sub-steps so the numbering does not shift:\n  - **Pointer read.** It is the first action inside the lock, before the similarity leftover cleanup. A missing file gives group 0. A changed N gives group 0, with \"N changed from X, restarting at 0\". A corrupt or unreadable file, non-JSON, a non-object, or a bad or boolean `increments`/`last_group` raises `RuntimeError` naming the file; fix or delete it.\n  - **Group filter.** It deletes the staging `instances` rows outside the group. It runs after `instances-cli` and the `--skip-local-dead` prune, and before `channels-cli`.\n  - **Pointer write.** It is atomic (mkstemp in the same directory, fsync, `os.replace`). It happens right after `merge-staging-db.py` returns success, before the post-merge denylist prune. A later failure does not hold the pointer back. A write `OSError` is logged, the post-merge steps (popularity, ANN, Engine start, crawl.db, trending, similarity) still run, and the run then fails with `RuntimeError(\"increment pointer not advanced: \u2026\")`, which takes precedence over a held trending error.\n- **Startup refusals.** Before the lock, the run refuses a negative `--increments`, `--increments` together with `--sync-join-whitelist`, and a state-file directory that does not exist.\n- **Group rule.**\n  - `int(sha1(host as stored, UTF-8)) % N`.\n  - It balances host counts, not crawl cost. The upgrade path is a persisted, size-balanced map.\n  - `--max-instances`/`--max-channels` now apply to the group.\n  - The instances stage still covers every host.\n  - New JoinPeerTube hosts are crawled on their group's day.\n- **Trending Stage (98).** \"With the weekly timer, a host that fails one run keeps its list and a host that fails two runs loses it\" is false. running post-merge steps before failing the run\" suffix on a write failure).\n  - `updater-worker.log` is append-only and unrotated, and now grows daily; suggest logrotate `copytruncate`.\n  - `catalog-update-*.log` files accumulate in the repo root; suggest a `find \u2026 -mtime +30 -delete` pruning line.\n- **Uninstall.** The pointer survives `--purge-updater-state`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DATA_BUILD.md\" update=\"yes\">\nLine 28, \"Timer runs weekly (`OnCalendar=Fri *-*-* 20:00:00` by default), so Trending is up to a week old\", is false. The real default is `--gpu --skip-local-dead --concurrency 5 --timeout-ms 15000 --max-retries 3 --increments 7`, and a custom value must keep `--increments`.\n- **Line 760.** \"the updater timer re-crawls weekly\" becomes daily, one seventh of the hosts per run.\n\nAdd two Triage rows:\n- the pointer-file `RuntimeError` before any crawl: fix or delete `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json`;\n- \"increment pointer not advanced\" after a merge, with the run failing at the end: check that the updater user can write to `engine/server/db/`, because the same group is re-crawled until it can.\n\nNear the uninstall example (483-485), optionally say that `--purge-updater-state` does not remove the pointer.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0010-trending-from-source-instances.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe 2026-10-03 Note (line 50) says the timer runs weekly (`Fri *-*-* 20:00:00`), that Trending is up to a week old, and that a failing host \"survives one failed weekly run and is dropped after two\". All three are false now. Add a dated Note (issue 63) and leave the old one as it is. The new note says:\n- the timer is daily, so decision 1's \"once a day\" holds again and Trending is at most a day old;\n- `AGE_OUT_MS` is still 10 days, so a failing host keeps its list through about nine consecutive failed daily runs.\n\nThat is a change to the issue 38 operator decision; see adr_conflicts.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"CONTEXT.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- **Trending entry (29).** \"the updater's weekly trending stage\" becomes \"daily\". The 10-day clause stays accurate.\n- **New glossary entry, Increment.** Define it as a fixed group of catalogue hosts (`sha1(host) % N`, N from `--increments`, 7 by default in the timer and `run-catalog-update.sh`) that one catalog update run crawls. The next group comes from `updater-increment.json`, which advances only after the run's merge commits. Keep it distinct from the `--incremental` modes of `recompute-popularity.py` and `precompute-similar-ann.py`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe issue is delivered:\n- Set Status to `enhancement, complete`.\n- Record what was delivered: `--increments N` / `--increment-state`; the sha1 group rule; the pointer file and its advance-after-merge rule; daily `*-*-* 20:00:00` timers and `run-catalog-update.sh` with `--increments 7`; the documented crontab line.\n- Record that \"a cron job runs the command once a week\" was superseded by daily runs of one seventh.\n- Move the issue to `docs/project/issues/archive/`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/issue-tracker.md\" update=\"yes\">\nRow 63 (line 11) still lists the issue as `ready`. Remove it when the issue moves to archive.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/roadmap.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- Add a DONE entry for issue 63: daily catalog update runs crawl one of 7 fixed host groups, with a pointer advanced after the merge. Point it at UPDATER_WORKER.md, the plan and the archived issue.\n- Line 37 says \"the updater's weekly trending stage\". The trending stage is now daily; change the word to \"daily\".\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/43-updater-trending-launch-failure-skips-similarity.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThis is an open issue, and line 14 says \"the weekly similarity rebuild is lost for that run\". The similarity rebuild now runs daily, so \"weekly\" becomes \"daily\". The held pointer-write error uses the same held-error pattern and changes nothing else in the analysis.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0005-raw-event-retention-keeps-ids.md\" update=\"no\">\nDecision 3's \"not the optional weekly updater\" is the historical rationale for pruning in the Engine. The decision does not depend on the updater's cadence, and the updater remains optional, so the decision is unaffected.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0009-engine-blue-green-through-nginx-upstream-snippet.md\" update=\"no\">\nIt says only that the updater stops and starts the Engine \"on its own schedule\", under the deploy lock. It states no cadence, and this build leaves the lock and the stop/start window unchanged.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"peertube-browser-service-review.md\" update=\"no\">\nThis is a point-in-time external review of the repo as it stood then (F4 quotes `OnCalendar=Fri *-*-* 20:00:00`). It is a dated assessment, not a maintained description of current behaviour, so it is not rewritten.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"README.md\" update=\"no\">\nIt mentions only `--purge-updater-state` / `--keep-updater-state` in the uninstall examples. It makes no claim about what the purge removes and says nothing about cadence or flags, so nothing in it became false. That the pointer survives the purge is documented in UPDATER_WORKER.md and DEPLOYMENT.md.\n</doc>\n</docs>\n\n<adr_conflicts>\nADR-0010 (Trending from source instances), the 2026-10-03 Note: it records the operator decision from issue 38 that the updater stays weekly and that the 10-day `AGE_OUT_MS` means a failing host \"survives one failed weekly run and is dropped after two\". This build changes the default timer to daily and leaves `AGE_OUT_MS` at 10 days. A failing host now keeps its trending list through about nine consecutive failed runs, and a list can be up to 10 days stale. Only the `fetch-trending.py` comment was updated. The operator must decide whether to keep 10 days and record that in a new dated ADR note, or to shorten `AGE_OUT_MS` (for example to about 2 days) to keep \"dropped after two failed runs\". Shortening it would change `tests/active/test_fetch_trending.py`'s 10-day pins. Decision 1's \"once a day\" is satisfied again, so on that point the build agrees with the ADR.\n</adr_conflicts>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md": "<changes>\nI updated `UPDATER_WORKER.md` to cover `--increments N` / `--increment-state` and the daily `--increments 7` schedule, and added a section on running it from cron. I checked each claim against `updater-worker.py`, `run-catalog-update.sh`, `run-services.sh`, `install-updater-service.sh`, `uninstall-service.sh`, `worktree-setup.sh`, `fetch-trending.py` and `.gitignore`.\n\n- **Purpose and Inputs/Outputs:** says a run can crawl one host group, adds the pointer file to the outputs, and says the staging DB is filtered to the group.\n- **Execution Order:** the step numbers are unchanged. New sub-steps:\n  - Step 1: the pointer is read first under the lock. A run refused at the lock never reads it.\n  - Step 5: the group filter runs after `--skip-local-dead` and before `channels-cli`.\n  - Step 8: the pointer is written once the merge child succeeds, before step 9.\n  - Step 15: a failed pointer write that was held back fails the run after the similarity stage, ahead of a held trending failure.\n- **New section \"Increments: One Host Group per Run\".** It has five parts:\n  - **Group rule:** sha1 of the host as stored, mod N. Groups balance host counts, not crawl cost, and the upgrade path is named. The instances stage still covers every host. `--max-instances` and `--max-channels` apply within the group. The global steps run on every run.\n  - **Startup refusals:** a negative N, `--increments` with `--sync-join-whitelist`, and a state directory that does not exist.\n  - **Pointer file:** path, example content, and that it and its temp file are gitignored. A worktree run, or any manual `--increments` run, uses main's pointer and takes the next group. `--purge-updater-state` leaves the file in place.\n  - **Reading:** a missing file gives group 0. A changed N gives group 0. Every kind of corrupt file gives a `RuntimeError` saying to fix or delete it.\n  - **Advancing:** the write is atomic. What leaves the pointer unchanged and what leaves it advanced. A write `OSError` is held back: the post-merge steps still run, then the run fails, and the same group is crawled again.\n- **Trending Stage:** at the daily cadence, a failing host keeps its list through about nine consecutive failed runs.\n- **Resume Staging:** the filter is applied again to a reused staging DB, and rows left by another group's run merge again harmlessly.\n- **Important Flags:** adds `--increments N` and `--increment-state PATH`.\n- **Manual Run:** the example now has `--increments 7`. `run-catalog-update.sh` passes `--increments 7`, and `-- --increments 0` forces a full crawl because the last occurrence of a flag wins.\n- **Systemd Run:**\n  - The timer is daily: `OnCalendar=*-*-* 20:00:00`.\n  - The real full `UPDATER_FLAGS` default is shown.\n  - A custom value has to keep `--increments 7`.\n  - Installed units only change when the installer is run again.\n- **New section \"Cron Run (no systemd)\":**\n  - The crontab line, with PATH taken from `dirname \"$(command -v node)\"`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` set, and output sent to `/dev/null`.\n  - Why the line must not contain `%` or `engine/server/api/server.py`.\n  - The script detaches and writes a timestamped log. A run that overlaps the previous one exits on the lock without touching the pointer. The repo does not install the line.\n  - The services are restarted through `run-services.sh`; the translate worker gets 120 s to stop and its in-flight job is requeued.\n  - A missing `.env.bridge`, `curl` or `ffmpeg` makes the restart fail.\n  - Sharing the GPU with the translate worker falls back to CPU.\n- **Logs:**\n  - The four `increment \u2026` log lines, in the exact format the code writes them.\n  - `updater-worker.log` is append-only and never rotated; a logrotate `copytruncate` example is given.\n  - A `find \u2026 -mtime +30 -delete` crontab line to prune `catalog-update-*.log`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DATA_BUILD.md": "<changes>\nI updated the `DATA_BUILD.md` updater bullet: the timer now runs daily with `--increments 7`, each host is refreshed about weekly, and Trending is up to a day old.\n\n- **Line 28.** It said the timer runs weekly (`OnCalendar=Fri *-*-* 20:00:00`) and that Trending is up to a week old. It now says the timer runs daily (`OnCalendar=*-*-* 20:00:00` by default) with `--increments 7`. Each run crawls one of 7 fixed host groups, so each host is refreshed about once a week. Trending is fetched from every host on every run, so it is up to a day old.\n- **Pointer sentence below the bullets.** It now lists \"host groups and the increment pointer\" among the topics `UPDATER_WORKER.md` covers. The group and pointer rules are only pointed at here, not repeated.\n- **Checked against the code.** Both installers default to `*-*-* 20:00:00`, and their default `UPDATER_FLAGS` end in `--increments 7`. `updater-worker.py` runs `fetch-trending.py` on every run.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DEPLOYMENT.md": "<changes>\nI updated DEPLOYMENT.md: the updater timer is now daily with `--increments 7` (each run crawls a seventh of the hosts), the `UPDATER_FLAGS` default is correct, and there are two new Triage rows for pointer-file failures.\n\n- **Units table:** the `peertube-updater.timer` row reads `OnCalendar=*-*-* 20:00:00`.\n- **\"The updater timer\" section:**\n  - It now runs daily and crawls one seventh of the catalogue hosts (`--increments 7`), so each host is refreshed about once a week.\n  - The ~1.5-minute Engine stop and the similarity build now happen once a day.\n  - The group rule and the pointer file `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json` (advanced only after the merge commits) are pointed at `UPDATER_WORKER.md`, not restated.\n- **`UPDATER_FLAGS` default:** the old text was wrong; it is now the real default, `--gpu --skip-local-dead --concurrency 5 --timeout-ms 15000 --max-retries 3 --increments 7`, checked against both installers. Two notes were added:\n  - a custom value has to keep `--increments 7`, or every daily run crawls every host;\n  - installed units only pick up new defaults when the installer is re-run.\n- **Firewall paragraph:** \"the updater timer re-crawls weekly\" now says it re-crawls one seventh of the hosts daily.\n- **Triage, two new rows:**\n  - The pointer file is corrupt or unreadable, so the run fails before any crawl. The symptom lists the worker's real messages (`increment pointer <path> is unreadable` / `is not a JSON object` / `has increments=\u2026` / `has last_group=\u2026`). The fix is to repair or delete the file; deleting it restarts at group 0.\n  - `increment pointer not advanced \u2026 ; running post-merge steps before failing the run`, then the run fails at the end. The fix is to make `engine/server/db/` writable by the updater's user; until then every run re-crawls the same group.\n- **Uninstall:** a line under the uninstall example says `--purge-updater-state` leaves the pointer file in place. I checked `scripts/uninstall-service.sh`: it only removes the week-state file.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/adr/0010-trending-from-source-instances.md": "<changes>\nAdded a dated Note (2026-10-15, issue 63) to ADR-0010 about the daily cadence. The 2026-10-03 Note is unchanged.\n\n- **Timer and crawl:** the timer runs daily (`*-*-* 20:00:00`) with `--increments 7`, so each run crawls one seventh of the hosts. The trending stage still fetches every host on every run; the code passes `fetch-trending.py` the prod DB without a host filter.\n- **Decision 1:** \"once a day\" holds as written again, and Trending is at most a day old.\n- **Age-out:** `AGE_OUT_MS` is still 10 days, so a host whose fetch fails keeps its list through about nine failed daily runs in a row. The note says this changes what issue 38's \"survives one failed run, dropped after two\" decision means in practice, and that choosing between the two is your call.\n- **Pointers:** the note links to `UPDATER_WORKER.md` for the increment rules and to plan `01-63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md`.\n\nI checked the facts against the code: the `UPDATER_TIMER_ONCALENDAR` defaults in both installers, `AGE_OUT_MS` and its comment in `fetch-trending.py`, and the trending call in `updater-worker.py`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:CONTEXT.md": "<changes>\nCONTEXT.md: the Trending entry now says the trending stage runs daily, and there is a new glossary entry for **Increment**.\n\n- **Trending entry:** \"the updater's weekly trending stage\" now reads \"daily\". The clause about the 10-day keep is unchanged, since it is still accurate.\n- **New Increment entry**, placed between Trending and Popular:\n  - It defines an increment as one fixed group of catalogue hosts, `sha1(host) % N`, taken over `instances.host` exactly as stored.\n  - N comes from `--increments`. It is 7 in the default timer and in `scripts/run-catalog-update.sh`, so on daily runs each host is refreshed about once a week.\n  - The run crawls the group after the one recorded in `updater-increment.json`. That pointer advances only after the run's merge into prod has committed, so a failed run retries the same group.\n  - The entry says an increment is not the same thing as the `--incremental` modes of `recompute-popularity.py` and `precompute-similar-ann.py`.\n  - It points to `engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md` for the pointer and filter rules instead of repeating them.\n- I checked the entry against the code: the sha1 rule (`host_increment_group`), `INCREMENT_STATE_NAME`, and the `--increments 7` and daily defaults in `scripts/install-service.sh` and `scripts/run-catalog-update.sh`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md": "<changes>\nI closed issue 63 in place: its status is `enhancement, complete`, and a dated comment under `## Comments` records what was delivered, pointing to the plan and its record.\n\n**You need to look at this.** The worker in the tree no longer writes the pointer the way the build delivered it. Line 1508 of `engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py` reads `write_increment_pointer(increment_state, (selected_group + 1) % args.increments, args.increments)`. The build diff (`build.diff:435`) and Phase 2's report both have `write_increment_pointer(increment_state, selected_group, args.increments)`, so this changed after this step began.\n\nAs it stands, the file records the next group instead of the one just crawled. Since `read_increment_pointer` adds 1 again, every run skips a group: the order is 0, 2, 4, \u2026. With N=7 every group is still reached, but `last_group` is wrong, and with an even N half the groups are never crawled. Phase 2's checkpoint asserts `written[\"last_group\"] == group`, so it would fail against this line. It may be a harvest mutation still in progress; if not, it needs reverting. The comment I wrote describes the delivered rule: the pointer records the last completed group.\n\n- **Status line:** changed from `enhancement, ready` to `enhancement, complete`. The category stays, and I matched the unquoted style the archived issues use.\n- **Comment, dated 2026-10-15:** it names `docs/project/plans/01-63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md` and its `.record.md`. It records:\n  - Daily runs that each crawl one seventh of the hosts replace \"a cron job runs the command once a week\", and each host is still refreshed about weekly.\n  - `--increments N` and the sha1 group rule. The other groups' staging rows are deleted before the channels stage, and 0 or absent means a full crawl.\n  - `--increment-state` and the pointer file. The pointer is written atomically only after the merge succeeds, a run that fails before or during the merge retries its group, and a corrupt pointer fails the run before any crawl.\n  - Both installers default to a daily `*-*-* 20:00:00` timer with `--increments 7`, and `run-catalog-update.sh` passes `--increments 7`. The comment points to `UPDATER_WORKER.md` for the crontab line instead of repeating it.\n  - The merge risk the issue raised did not hold: `merge-staging-db.py` never deletes, so a host missing from staging keeps its prod rows.\n- I checked these facts in the tree: the `read_increment_pointer` rules, the startup refusals, and the `UPDATER_TIMER_ONCALENDAR`/`UPDATER_FLAGS` defaults in both installers and in `run-catalog-update.sh`.\n- I did not touch the tracker row (its own checklist item), any links elsewhere, or the archive move, which the workflow does itself.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/issue-tracker.md": "<changes>\nRemoved row 63 (\"Run the catalog update in weekly increments\") from the open-issues table, because the issue is delivered and is being archived.\n\n- I deleted only that row. The other rows, the header and the intro are unchanged.\n- The deleted row was the table's only link to `63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md`, so nothing in this file needs repointing to `archive/`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/roadmap.md": "<changes>\nI added a DONE entry for issue 63 to the roadmap and changed the issue 38 entry's \"weekly trending stage\" to \"daily\".\n\n- **New entry under \"Delivered\"**, placed after issue 42's entry: \"DONE \u2014 **Issue `63`, catalog update in daily increments**\". It says the updater timer and `scripts/run-catalog-update.sh` run daily with `--increments 7`. Each run crawls one of 7 fixed host groups, so each host is refreshed about once a week. A pointer file selects the next group and only advances after the run's merge commits.\n- **Where it points:** the group and pointer rules are left to `engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md`. The entry also links the plan `docs/project/plans/01-63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md` and the issue at its archive path `docs/project/issues/archive/63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md`. That link resolves once the workflow moves the issue there.\n- **Checked against the code:** the defaults `*-*-* 20:00:00` and `--increments 7` are in `engine/install-updater-service.sh`, `--increments 7` is in `scripts/run-catalog-update.sh`, and the pointer file name `updater-increment.json` is in `updater-worker.py`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/43-updater-trending-launch-failure-skips-similarity.md": "<changes>\nIssue 43 now calls the similarity rebuild \"daily\" instead of \"weekly\", since the updater timer runs every day.\n\n- Line 14: \"the weekly similarity rebuild is lost for that run\" now reads \"the daily similarity rebuild is lost for that run\".\n- I checked the rest of the issue against the code and left it as it was. The default `UPDATER_TIMER_ONCALENDAR` is `*-*-* 20:00:00`. In `updater-worker.py`, the code around the trending `run_cmd` (line 1615) still catches only `subprocess.CalledProcessError`, and `RuntimeError(\"trending stage failed\")` is still raised from the held error (line 1638). The bug, how likely it is and the proposed fix are all still accurate. The held pointer-write error is raised ahead of a held trending error, but that doesn't change this issue's analysis.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",

It was renamed after taking on the archived dev test's two claims: the exact single-name `stop|start peertube-engine-dev` sudoers rule, and the exact `ExecStart` with no `--engine-upstream-snippet`, re-pinned to end `--max-retries 3 --increments 7'`.\ntests/tmp/test_63_catalog_update_weekly_increments_phase4.py::test_catalog_update_passes_increments_seven_ahead_of_operator_flags_so_increments_zero_overrides -> tests/active/test_run_catalog_update.py (NEW group test_run_catalog_update.py)\ntests/tmp/test_63_catalog_update_weekly_increments_phase4.py::test_catalog_update_without_operator_flags_passes_increments_seven -> tests/active/test_run_catalog_update.py (NEW group test_run_catalog_update.py)\nName checks (also recorded in HARVEST_FILE):\n- test_updater_worker.py:\n  - kept the active `ROOT`, `SERVER_DIR`, `JOBS_DIR`, `PYTHON_BIN`, `_load_job`, `updater` and `_jobs`; dropped the incoming `_jobs` and `JOB_SCRIPTS`;\n  - kept one copy each of `_is`, `_snapshot`, `_pointer`, `_messages`, `NOT_ADVANCED` and `PRIOR_POINTER` (phase 1's `VALID_POINTER` became `PRIOR_POINTER`);\n  - renamed phase 1 `_run_crawl_main` to `_run_increment_crawl_main` and phase 1 `HOSTS` to `GROUP_HOSTS`, and phase 3 `_run_increment_main` to `_run_increment_main_with_similarity`;\n  - added an increments paragraph to the module docstring.\n- test_install_updater_service.py: kept the active `worker`; added `DAILY`, `_parse` and `_on_calendar`; `harness.X` references became direct names; reworded the docstring (line 1, and the old dev line 4).\n- test_run_catalog_update.py: `BASH`, `UPDATER_WORKER`, `_values`, `worker`, `_parse`, `RECORDER`, `CATALOG_SCRIPT` and `_run_catalog_update` are copied in, not imported.\nPre-harvest record: there was no `.preharvest` file. So I copied the record to `tests/last_test_validation.json.preharvest` (`cmp` clean) before any banking run, and Step 8 restored that copy.\n</moved>\n\n<retired>\ntests/active/test_install_updater_service.py::test_updater_installer_dev_dry_run_keeps_single_name_rule: a builder cut it mid-build (phase 4) into tests/archive/01-63-catalog-update-weekly-increments/test_install_updater_service.py, with a README.md. The whole run is under `single_run_lock` (`/tmp/peertube-browser-staging-sync.lock`); a second run while one is live raises `RuntimeError` and exits non-zero.\n- Every crawl stage takes its hosts from the staging `instances` table: `channels-worker.ts` (`store.listInstances()`), `videos-worker.ts` (`store.listInstances()`, then `listChannelsWithVideos(1, hosts)`), `channels-videos-count-worker.ts` (`store.listInstances()`). The shim's `stop` records \"Engine was running\" from that match, and `start` restarts services only if it was.\n- `run-catalog-update.sh` needs `node` (and `npm` unless `--skip-build`) on PATH and exits FAILED otherwise. It resolves python itself from the pixi env or venv.\n\n### Requirements\n\n1. **Opt-in flag.** `updater-worker.py` gains `--increments N` (integer; 0 or absent means off). Off: the run crawls every host exactly as today, unchanged. On: the run crawls only one group of hosts, as below. N must be at least 1 (N = 1 behaves like a full crawl but still uses the pointer).\n2. **Group assignment.** A host's group is `int(sha1(host).hexdigest(), 16) % N`, over the host string exactly as stored in `instances.host` (already lowercased and normalised by `normalize_host_token` / `normalizeHostToken`, UTF-8 encoded). Any failure before or during the merge leaves it unchanged, and the next run retries the same group. One side observation, not to be fixed here: `channels` is INSERT_ONLY, so the channel video counts the counts stage refreshes on seeded channels that already exist in prod do not reach prod.\n- Moving the updater's bare `urlopen` onto the source-fetch adapter.",

  "initial_solution": "### Approach\n\nAll the behaviour goes into `engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py`, as a few small module-level helpers in the same style as `prune_staging_local_non_ok_instances` and `purge_hosts_from_staging`. The rest is defaults, one test, and docs. No new module, no new dependency: `hashlib`, `json`, `os` and `tempfile` from the stdlib are enough.\n\n**Flags (req 1, 8).** `parse_args` gains `--increments` (int, default 0) and `--increment-state` (path, default unset). In `main()`, the state path defaults to `prod_db.parent / \"updater-increment.json\"`, so it sits next to whatever `--prod-db` names. That gives `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json` in production and keeps tests from touching the real file. Startup validation goes next to the existing `--dry-run` check, before the lock: a negative N is rejected, and N \u2265 1 together with `--sync-join-whitelist` is rejected with a clear error. With N = 0 nothing below runs and the code path is byte-for-byte today's.\n\n**Group function (req 2).** One helper returns `int(hashlib.sha1(host.encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest(), 16) % n`. It is computed in Python because SQLite has no sha1. The input is the host string exactly as stored in `instances.host`, with no re-normalisation, so the stored value is the only source of truth.\n\n**Pointer read (req 3).** It is read inside `single_run_lock`, as the first thing after the lock is taken and before cleanup, seeding or any crawl, so two runs can never interleave a read and a write. A missing file selects group 0. A file that parses but whose stored N differs from `--increments` selects group 0 and logs that the N changed. Otherwise the run takes `(last + 1) % N`. These cases raise `RuntimeError` naming the file and telling the operator to fix or delete it:\n- the file cannot be read or is not valid JSON;\n- it lacks `last_group` / `increments`;\n- `increments` is not an int \u2265 1;\n- `last_group` is not an int in `[0, increments)`.\n\nNothing is reset silently. The file holds `last_group`, `increments` and `completed_at` (UTC ISO timestamp).\n\n**Filter point (req 5).** A new helper sits after `run_cmd(instances_cmd)` and after the `--skip-local-dead` prune, before `channels_cmd`. The staging denylist prune already runs earlier, before the instances stage. The helper:\n1. reads every `host` from staging `instances`;\n2. keeps those whose group equals the selected one;\n3. deletes the rest in one transaction, by `executemany` on the host key;\n4. counts staging `channels` rows for the kept hosts;\n5. returns the kept-host and channel counts.\n\nThis is the same mechanism as the local-health prune, so every later crawl stage (each reads `store.listInstances()`) only sees the group. It runs whether staging was freshly seeded or reused with `--resume-staging`. On reuse the staging DB normally comes from a failed run of the same group, because the pointer did not advance, but the filter is re-applied regardless. Seeded `channels` rows of other hosts stay in staging and are harmless, as the requirement states.\n\n**Pointer advance (req 4).** The write goes immediately after the `merge-staging-db.py` `run_cmd` returns. That script commits its whole merge in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` \u2026 `commit` transaction and rolls back on error, so exit 0 means committed. The write comes before the post-merge denylist prune and is atomic: a temp file in the same directory, flushed and fsynced, then `os.replace`. Every failure before that line raises before the write and leaves the file alone:\n- a non-zero crawl CLI exit;\n- embeddings failing on both GPU and CPU (`run_with_cpu_fallback` raises);\n- `--fail-before-merge`;\n- a merge error;\n- refusal by the lock, which happens before the pointer is even read.\n\nFailures after it (prune, popularity, ANN, copy, trending, similarity) cannot reach back to undo it. If the write itself fails with an `OSError`, the error is logged as \"pointer not advanced\" and the global steps still run, so the ANN index matches prod. The run then exits non-zero at the end, the same way `trending_error` is held. The next run safely re-crawls the same group, because the INSERT_ONLY merge is idempotent.\n\n**Global steps (req 6).** These are unchanged and still run every time. Only their frequency changes, through the schedule.\n\n**Logging (req 7).** Each incremental run logs to the worker log:\n- one line at read time: N, the stored pointer (or \"missing\" / \"N changed from X, restarting at 0\"), and the selected group;\n- one line after the filter: group, hosts kept, hosts removed, staging channels for the group;\n- one line at the end: \"pointer written last_group=g\", or \"pointer not advanced: <reason>\" logged from the existing exception path. A failure before the merge logs that reason before re-raising. This is a small `try/except` that logs and re-raises around the pre-merge section, guarded on N \u2265 1, rather than restructuring `main()`.\n\n**Wiring (req 9).**\n- `scripts/run-catalog-update.sh`: `--increments 7` is added to the hard-coded worker flags, before `EXTRA_ARGS`. Argparse keeps the last occurrence, so `-- --increments 0` still forces a full crawl. The help header says both. Its `sed -n '2,23p'` range moves if the header grows.\n- Both installers: `UPDATER_FLAGS` gains `--increments 7` and `UPDATER_TIMER_ONCALENDAR` defaults to `*-*-* 20:00:00`. Both env/flag overrides are unchanged.\n- `tests/active/test_install_updater_service.py`: the pinned ExecStart and OnCalendar expectations get the new defaults. Its `parse_args` round-trip then also proves the worker accepts the flag.\n\n**Cron (req 10).** `UPDATER_WORKER.md` documents one line of the form `0 20 * * * PATH=<dir of node>:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin /usr/bin/bash /home/enduser/code/PeerTube-browser/scripts/run-catalog-update.sh >/dev/null 2>&1`. The doc tells the operator to substitute `dirname \"$(command -v node)\"`, which matters for nvm installs. The line names only the script path, so neither it nor the `/bin/sh -c` cron spawns contains `engine/server/api/server.py`. It avoids `%`, which cron treats specially. The script's own detached mode still writes `catalog-update-<timestamp>.log`. The redirect only stops cron mailing the two \"started\" lines. Overlap: the second run hits `single_run_lock` and exits non-zero before reading the pointer. Under systemd, a timer does not start a oneshot service that is still running.\n\n**Docs (req 11).**\n- `DATA_BUILD.md`: weekly becomes daily-by-seventh, and trending becomes \"up to a day old\".\n- `DEPLOYMENT.md`: timer table updated.\n- `UPDATER_WORKER.md`: flag, group rule, pointer file and advance rule, filter point, schedule, cron line, how to force a full crawl, and the simplification with its upgrade path.\n- ADR 0010: the cadence paragraph changes to daily.\n- `CONTEXT.md`: an \"increment\" glossary entry, because the build introduces the term in a flag name, a state file and the docs.\n\n### Alternatives considered\n\n- **Pass the group to the crawlers as a host list** (an include file, or the complement written into `--exclude-hosts-file`). Rejected: it needs TypeScript changes in three or four CLIs, or overloads the denylist file's meaning, and the out-of-group rows would still sit in staging and reach the merge. Deleting from staging uses a mechanism the worker already relies on.\n- **Filter at seed time** (seed only group hosts). Rejected: `instances-cli --whitelist-url` re-inserts every JoinPeerTube host afterwards, so a post-instances filter is needed anyway, and filtering twice is redundant.\n- **Derive the group from the date** (day-of-year % 7), with no state file. Rejected: a failed run would silently skip its group for a week. The settled pointer-plus-retry rule requires state.\n- **A stored host-to-group map.** Rejected for now as the named upgrade path; a hash needs no storage and handles new hosts automatically.\n- **Advance the pointer at the end of the run.** Rejected by req 4: a post-merge failure would make the next run re-crawl a group whose data is already in prod.\n\n### Risks and gotchas\n\n- **The instances stage stays global.** Every run still fetches the JoinPeerTube list and probes every instance before filtering. That stage was not the bulk (channels and videos were), but it is not divided by 7.\n- **`--max-instances` / `--max-channels` caps** now apply to the group subset, not the whole set. Same values, different meaning; worth a doc line.\n- **Imbalance.** A group holding several very large instances runs longer than a seventh. This is the deliberate simplification of req 2.\n- **Host normalisation drift.** If a host's stored string ever changed (e.g. a normalisation fix), it would move group. Harmless: at worst one host is crawled a few days early or late once.\n- **Changing N** restarts at group 0, so groups near the end of the old cycle wait up to a full cycle. This is logged.\n- **New JoinPeerTube hosts** reach prod only on their group's day, up to a week later than today's weekly-but-full run in the worst case. Accepted by req 2.\n- **Write failure after merge.** If the pointer write fails after a committed merge, the run is marked failed but the global steps still run. The group repeats next day, at the cost of one redundant crawl.\n- **Deleting the state file by hand** restarts at group 0. That is harmless, and documented as the recovery for a corrupt file.\n\n### Tradeoffs the operator accepts\n\n- The Engine stop window (~1.5 min) and the 30\u201340 min similarity build happen daily instead of weekly (req 6).\n- Daily runs mean daily GPU use and daily embeddings/ANN rebuilds of the whole prod index. The full ANN rebuild does not shrink with the crawl.\n- Per-host freshness stays about weekly, but varies per host: each host's day is fixed by its hash, not chosen.\n- Hosts that error inside a completed crawl wait a full cycle (req 4).\n- The non-systemd path depends on an operator-installed crontab line that the repo does not manage.",

See the main() entries.\n- **New tests.** They fit beside `_run_crawl_main` (937-977), which runs the full crawl path (not sync-join) to `--fail-before-merge` with only `subprocess.run` faked. A new full-crawl harness with `--skip-systemctl`, faking the merge child as exit 0, is required to observe the write after the merge and a held error after a forced `OSError` (for example a `--increment-state` in an unwritable or missing directory).\n- **Docstring.** The module docstring (1-32) lists every proven clause, the repo convention, so the new clauses go there.\n\n**What depends on it.** The durable suite.\n\n**Regression risk.** Medium. A main() restructure that breaks the AST scans fails here first, which is the intended guard.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"tests/active/test_host_normalisation.py\" element=\"_load_job of updater-worker.py (line 87), fetch_join_hosts check (111-115)\">\n**What changes.** Nothing.\n\n**Why it matters.** It execs the module, so a new import must be stdlib-only. `hashlib` is.\n\n**Regression risk.** None.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"tests/active/test_fetch_trending.py\" element=\"10-day age-out tests (docstring lines 1-5, test at 140)\">\n**What changes.** Nothing, unless the operator decides to change `AGE_OUT_MS` for the daily cadence (see the `fetch-trending.py` entry). In that case these pins move.\n\n**Regression risk.** None as planned.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"tests/config.json\" element=\"test map entries (test_updater_worker.py at line 304, test_install_updater_service.py at line 348)\">\n**What changes.** Only if the new incremental tests go into a new test file. That file then needs a map entry listing `engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py` (and, if the test reads it, `engine/crawler/schema.sql`). Tests added to `test_updater_worker.py` need no change.\n\n**Regression risk.** Low. A missing entry means the durable-suite map does not route updater changes to the new test.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/db/jobs/tests/test-orchestrator-smoke.py\" element=\"run_orchestrator worker argv (lines 415-473)\">\n**What changes.** Nothing. It passes no `--increments`, so the worker runs as today (N = 0). It is not in `tests/config.json`, so it is not part of the durable suite. An optional incremental scenario could be added later through its `extra_flags`.\n\n**Regression risk.** None.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\".gitignore\" element=\"local data files section (lines 10-25)\">\n**What changes.** The plan misses this. The new state file `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json` is not covered by any pattern: `*.db*`, `*.faiss.json` and the explicit lock files do not match it, and `*.json` is not ignored. Every dev checkout, and the prod checkout that runs from the repo directory, would then show it as untracked, and it could be committed by accident. The same goes for a leftover temp file from the atomic write. Add an entry, with a comment like the existing lock-file entries (lines 20-23), for `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json`, plus the temp-file pattern the write helper uses (for example `engine/server/db/updater-increment.*.tmp`).\n\n**Regression risk.** Low, but a committed pointer file would reset or skew other checkouts' groups.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"scripts/uninstall-service.sh\" element=\"--purge-updater-state / week_state_file (lines 155-199)\">\n**What changes.** The plan does not mention it, and I recommend no code change, only awareness. `--purge-updater-state` removes a legacy `/var/lib/peertube-browser/updater-last-success-week.txt`, which no current code writes (grep finds it only here, in `tests/run-installers-smoke.sh` and `peertube-browser-service-review.md`). It does not remove the new `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json`.\n\nAn operator reading \"purge updater state\" may expect the pointer to go. Either document that the pointer survives uninstall (harmless: a reinstall resumes the cycle), or extend the purge to it. Extending it would change `tests/run-installers-smoke.sh`'s expectations, so it is not recommended in this build.\n\n**Regression risk.** None if unchanged.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"scripts/run-services.sh\" element=\"stop_one / status pgrep patterns (lines 216-267)\">\n**What changes.** Nothing.\n\n**Why it matters.** It matches the Engine with `pgrep -f \"engine/server/api/server.py\"` (231, 245-260). Req 10's crontab line must not contain that string, and the planned line, which names only `scripts/run-catalog-update.sh`, does not.\n\n**Regression risk.** None. A crontab line that ran the worker directly with a path argument containing the Engine path would make `stop` kill the wrong process, which the doc should warn against.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"scripts/worktree-setup.sh\" element=\"whitelist.db symlink (lines 27-28)\">\n**What changes.** Nothing.\n\n**Why it matters.** The worker `.resolve()`s `--prod-db`, so in a worktree the default state path lands in main's `engine/server/db/`. A catalog update run from a worktree reads and advances main's pointer. That is consistent, since the dataset is the same, but surprising. Worth a line in UPDATER_WORKER.md.\n\n**Regression risk.** Low. Tests always pass a tmp `--prod-db`, so they never touch it.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/db/updater-increment.json\" element=\"new runtime artifact (pointer state file)\">\n**What changes.** A new file, created by the first successful incremental run. Its content is `{\"last_group\": int, \"increments\": int, \"completed_at\": \"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ\"}`. Deleting it by hand restarts at group 0, the documented recovery for a corrupt file.\n\n**What depends on it.** Every incremental run reads it under the lock. The file is owned by the user the run executes as: systemd's `SERVICE_USER`, or the cron user. If both paths are ever used with different users, the write fails with an `OSError` after the merge, and the run then re-crawls the same group daily until the owner is fixed.\n\n**Regression risk.** Low. The ownership mismatch is worth a Triage row.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md\" element=\"Purpose/Inputs-Outputs (5-36), Execution Order (42-89), Trending Stage write bullet (98), Important Flags (209-238), Manual Run (240-246), Systemd Run (248-272), Logs (274-297)\">\n**What changes.**\n- **Execution Order.** Steps are cross-referenced by number only inside this file (steps 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 15.4); no other doc cites them. Add the new steps as sub-steps (for example 1a pointer read, 5a group filter, 8a pointer write) so the numbering does not shift.\n- **Other sections.** See the docs checklist.\n\n**Regression risk.** Documentation only.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"DATA_BUILD.md\" element=\"Automatic background updater (line 28)\">\n**What changes.** The line \"Timer runs weekly (`OnCalendar=Fri *-*-* 20:00:00` by default), so Trending is up to a week old\" becomes daily (`*-*-* 20:00:00`) with `--increments 7`: each run crawls one seventh of the hosts, so each host is refreshed about weekly, and Trending is up to a day old.\n\n**Regression risk.** Documentation only.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"DEPLOYMENT.md\" element=\"units table (131), The updater timer (214, 228), outbound-443 paragraph (760), Triage table (~330-351)\">\n**What changes.**\n- Line 131: `OnCalendar=*-*-* 20:00:00`.\n- Line 214: \"Weekly, it crawls\" becomes \"Daily, it crawls one seventh of the hosts (`--increments 7`)\".\n- Line 228: `UPDATER_FLAGS` defaults are already stale (missing `--timeout-ms 15000 --max-retries 3`); give the full new default including `--increments 7`, and say a custom value must keep it.\n- Line 760: \"the updater timer re-crawls weekly\" becomes \"daily, one seventh of the hosts per run\".\n- Optional Triage rows: the corrupt or unreadable pointer `RuntimeError` (fix or delete the file), and \"pointer not advanced\" after a merge (permissions on `engine/server/db/`).\n\n**Regression risk.** Documentation only.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"docs/project/adr/0010-trending-from-source-instances.md\" element=\"Note (2026-10-03) paragraph (line 50)\">\n**What changes.** The note says the timer is weekly, so Trending is up to a week old, and that a failing host \"survives one failed weekly run and is dropped after two\". With daily runs, decision 1's \"once a day\" holds again, and Trending is at most a day old. That matches Consequences line 43.\n\nThe age-out sentence becomes \"survives about nine consecutive failed daily runs\", unless `AGE_OUT_MS` changes. That is a change to the operator decision recorded via issue 38, so surface it rather than silently rewriting. Add a dated note (for example \"Note (issue 63): daily cadence\") rather than editing the old one, matching ADR practice.\n\n**Regression risk.** Documentation only, but it is an ADR conflict to flag.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"CONTEXT.md\" element=\"Trending entry (line 29), new Increment entry\">\n**What changes.**\n- **Trending entry.** It says \"by the updater's weekly trending stage; a host that fails a run keeps its list until it is more than 10 days old\". Update \"weekly\" to \"daily\". The 10-day clause stays accurate as long as `AGE_OUT_MS` is unchanged.\n- **New entry.** Add an **Increment** entry: \"a fixed group of catalogue hosts, chosen by `sha1(host) % N`, that one catalog update run crawls; N is `--increments` (7 by default in the timer and `run-catalog-update.sh`); the next group comes from a pointer file advanced only after the run's merge commits\". It must be distinct from the unrelated `--incremental` flags of `recompute-popularity.py` and `precompute-similar-ann.py`, a real confusion risk worth one clause.\n\n**Regression risk.** Documentation only.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"docs/project/adr/0005-raw-event-retention-keeps-ids.md\" element=\"decision 3 (line 15) 'not the optional weekly updater'\">\n**What changes.** Nothing recommended. It is a historical rationale, and the decision (pruning in the Engine) is unaffected by a daily updater. Listed so the next step does not take it for an omission.\n\n**Regression risk.** None.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"docs/project/issues/43-updater-trending-launch-failure-skips-similarity.md\" element=\"likelihood paragraph (line 14) 'the weekly similarity rebuild is lost'\">\n**What changes.** Optional: \"weekly\" becomes \"daily\", which lowers the cost of that open bug. The new held pointer-write error follows the same held-error pattern as `trending_error`, so it does not change issue 43's analysis.\n\n**Regression risk.** None.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"docs/project/issues/63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md\" element=\"Status line, delivery\">\n**What changes.** On delivery, set the Status to `complete`, record what was delivered (daily runs, 7 groups, pointer file, cron line), and move the issue to `docs/project/issues/archive/` per the tracker rules.\n\n**Regression risk.** None.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"docs/project/issues/issue-tracker.md\" element=\"row 63 (line 11)\">\n**What changes.** Remove the row when issue 63 moves to `archive/`.\n\n**Regression risk.** None.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"docs/project/roadmap.md\" element=\"DONE list (around line 37)\">\n**What changes.**\n- Add a DONE entry for issue 63, like the other delivered issues, pointing at UPDATER_WORKER.md and the plan.\n- Line 37's \"fetched by the updater's weekly trending stage\" is history in a DONE entry; update it to \"daily\" or leave it, as the operator prefers.\n\n**Regression risk.** None.\n</impact>\n</impacts>\n\n<impact path=\"scripts/run-services.sh\" element=\"start_services / stop_services as called by the catalog-update shim (lines 143-198, 227-232; header line 8)\">\n**What changes.** No code change is planned. What changes is how often this runs and who is watching. On the cron path, the `systemctl` shim that `run-catalog-update.sh` writes (lines 98-115) turns the worker's Engine `stop` into `bash run-services.sh stop`, and its `start` into `bash run-services.sh start`. The `start` only happens when the Engine was running at stop time (STATE_FILE, line 103/107). I checked what that does here:\n- **The stop affects all three services.** `stop_services` (227-232) stops the translate worker first, with SIGTERM and up to `WORKER_STOP_TIMEOUT=120` s (line 43). The comment at 41-42 says an in-flight job is requeued; a SIGKILL after 120 s leaves it `running` and costs a claim. It then stops the Client and the Engine. So every cron run also stops the Client and the translate worker for the merge, popularity and ANN window, not only the Engine.\n- **The start can fail with no one watching.** `start_services` (143-198) needs `.env.bridge`, through `load_bridge_secret`, which `exit 1`s when the file is missing (95-111). It needs `curl` for `health_status` (124). It needs the Engine healthy within `HEALTH_TIMEOUT=300` s, and the translate worker alive 3 s after launch (it exits at once without ffmpeg, line 187-194). Any of these failing leaves the Client or the translate worker down after an unattended daily run. `run-catalog-update.sh:130-133` only re-checks the Engine, and only by `pgrep`, so a Client or translate-worker failure shows only in the detached log.\n- **The relaunch runs in cron's environment.** Line 8 asks the operator to set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to pin the translate worker. The worker relaunched at line 185 inherits cron's minimal environment, so the pin is lost unless the crontab line sets it. Setting it in the crontab line has a side effect: it is also inherited by `updater-worker.py` and its embeddings, ANN and similarity children, so the updater's `--gpu` work is pinned to the same card.\n- **GPU overlap.** Embeddings run before the Engine stop, and the similarity build runs after the start. The translate worker is running during both, so they compete with it for VRAM. A GPU failure there is retried on CPU by `run_with_cpu_fallback` (updater-worker.py:414-432) and logged, but the run does not fail. Today this happens weekly; with the plan it happens daily.\n\n**What depends on it.** The cron line documented in UPDATER_WORKER.md (req 10), the translate worker's job queue, and the Client's availability. The systemd path is unaffected: there the worker calls real `systemctl` on the Engine units only.\n\n**Regression risk.** Medium in operations, none in code. Nothing in the build changes this file. The risk is an undocumented daily restart of three services from a bare environment. Document in the cron section that each run restarts the Client and the translate worker (an in-flight translation is requeued). The crontab line must carry the environment the services need, such as `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<uuid>`, accepting that it also pins the updater. Point to `catalog-update-*.log` for restart failures.\n</impact>\n\n<impact path=\"scripts/run-catalog-update.sh\" element=\"\">\n.log (lines 20-21, 51-56)\">\n**What changes.** No code change is planned. Each detached run writes a new `${REPO_DIR}/catalog-update-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log` (line 52) in the repo root. With a daily cron that is about 365 files a year, and nothing prunes them. `.gitignore` line 3 (`*.log`) keeps them out of git. The cron line's `>/dev/null 2>&1` only discards the two \"started\" lines (54-55); the whole run, including `run-services.sh` restart failures, goes to this file.\n\n**What depends on it.** It is the operator's only record of a cron run's shim and service-restart output; the worker's own lines also go to `updater-worker.log`.\n\n**Regression risk.** Low: disk use and clutter in the repo root. Add a doc line in UPDATER_WORKER.md (cron section and Logs) telling the operator to prune these files periodically, for example `find <repo> -maxdepth 1 -name 'catalog-update-*.log' -mtime +30 -delete`, as a separate crontab line (it contains no `%`). Pruning in the script is an upgrade path and is not recommended in this build.\n</impact>\n\n<impact path=\"engine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py\" element=\"setup_logging (lines 322-330) and default --logs path (line 111)\">\n**What changes.** Nothing in code. `setup_logging` attaches a plain `logging.FileHandler(log_path, \"a\")` (325) to `engine/server/db/updater-worker.log` (default at line 111). This happens on both the systemd and cron paths, in addition to the journal or stdout. With daily runs the file grows about seven times as fast as today, and nothing rotates it. The `*.log` pattern keeps it out of git. The three new log lines (pointer read, group filter, pointer written / not advanced) add to it.\n\n**What depends on it.** Operators reading the worker log (UPDATER_WORKER.md Logs, 274-278). Three test files exec this module (`test_updater_worker.py`, `test_host_normalisation.py:87`, `test_install_updater_service.py:93`), and `test_updater_worker.py` reads log output from `main()` runs.\n\n**Regression risk.** Low. Switching to `RotatingFileHandler` is out of scope, and it would touch logging that those tests exercise. Add a doc line in the Logs section saying the file is append-only and unrotated, and how to truncate or rotate it (for example a logrotate `copytruncate` rule, or truncating it between runs).\n</impact>",
  "docs_checklist": "- [x] `engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md` - updated: I updated `UPDATER_WORKER.md` to cover `--increments N` / `--increment-state` and the daily `--increments 7` schedule, and added a section on running it from cron. The 2026-10-03 Note is unchanged.\n- [x] `CONTEXT.md` - updated: CONTEXT.md: the Trending entry now says the trending stage runs daily, and there is a new glossary entry for **Increment**.\n- [x] `docs/project/issues/63-catalog-update-weekly-increments.md` - updated: I closed issue 63 in place: its status is `enhancement, complete`, and a dated comment under `## Comments` records what was delivered, pointing to the plan and its record.\n- [x] `docs/project/issues/issue-tracker.md` - updated: Removed row 63 (\"Run the catalog update in weekly increments\") from the open-issues table, because the issue is delivered and is being archived.\n- [x] `docs/project/roadmap.md` - updated: I added a DONE entry for issue 63 to the roadmap and changed the issue 38 entry's \"weekly trending stage\" to \"daily\".\n- [x] `docs/project/issues/43-updater-trending-launch-failure-skips-similarity.md` - updated: Issue 43 now calls the similarity rebuild \"daily\" instead of \"weekly\", since the updater timer runs every day.\n- [x] `docs/project/adr/0005-raw-event-retention-keeps-ids.md` - out of scope: Decision 3's \"not the optional weekly updater\" is the historical rationale for pruning in the Engine. The decision does not depend on the updater's cadence, and the updater remains optional, so the decision is unaffected.\n- [x] `docs/project/adr/0009-engine-blue-green-through-nginx-upstream-snippet.md` - out of scope: It says only that the updater stops and starts the Engine \"on its own schedule\", under the deploy lock. It states no cadence, and this build leaves the lock and the stop/start window unchanged.\n- [x] `peertube-browser-service-review.md` - out of scope: This is a point-in-time external review of the repo as it stood then (F4 quotes `OnCalendar=Fri *-*-* 20:00:00`). It is a dated assessment, not a maintained description of current behaviour, so it is not rewritten.\n- [x] `README.md` - out of scope: It mentions only `--purge-updater-state` / `--keep-updater-state` in the uninstall examples.     {
      "path": "engine/server/db/jobs/docs/UPDATER_WORKER.md",
      "note": "**Purpose and Outputs (5-36):**\n- Name the per-run host group.\n- Add the pointer file `engine/server/db/updater-increment.json` as persistent state. It sits next to `--prod-db` and is overridable with `--increment-state`.\n- Name its temp file.\n- Say that the staging DB, though \"recreated each run\", is filtered to the group.\n\n**Execution Order (42-89):** add sub-steps rather than renumbering:\n- Read the pointer right after the lock, before cleanup. A missing file selects group 0. A changed N selects group 0 and is logged. A corrupt file raises `RuntimeError`; fix or delete the file.\n- Filter staging `instances` to the group after `instances-cli` and the `--skip-local-dead` prune, before `channels-cli`.\n- Write the pointer atomically right after the merge commits, before the post-merge denylist prune. Failures after the write do not hold it back. A write `OSError` is logged, the global steps still run, and the run exits non-zero at the end.\n\n**Group rule:**\n- `sha1(host) % N` over the stored `instances.host` string.\n- The deliberate simplification: groups balance host counts, not crawl cost. The upgrade path is a persisted, size-balanced host-to-group map.\n- The `--max-instances`/`--max-channels` caps now apply to the group.\n- The instances stage still covers every host.\n- `--increments` is refused with `--sync-join-whitelist`.\n\n**Trending Stage (98):** replace \"With the weekly timer, a host that fails one run keeps its list and a host that fails two runs loses it\" with what the 10-day window means at a daily cadence, or with the new window if the operator changes it.\n\n**Resume Staging Behavior:** the filter is re-applied to a reused staging DB. That DB may still hold another group's merged rows, which re-merge harmlessly.\n\n**Important Flags:** add `--increments N` (0 = full crawl, the worker default) and `--increment-state PATH`.\n\n**Manual Run:** show `--increments 7`. Show that `--increments 0`, or `scripts/run-catalog-update.sh -- --increments 0`, forces a full crawl.\n\n**Systemd Run (248-272):**\n- \"(weekly schedule)\" becomes daily.\n- `OnCalendar=*-*-* 20:00:00`.\n- The flags example gains `--increments 7`.\n- Warn that a custom `UPDATER_FLAGS` must keep `--increments`, or every daily run crawls everything.\n\n**New \"Cron (no systemd)\" section:**\n- The exact line: `0 20 * * * PATH=<dir of node>:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin /usr/bin/bash <repo>/scripts/run-catalog-update.sh >/dev/null 2>&1`. Take `<dir of node>` from `dirname \"$(command -v node)\"` (nvm installs).\n- Avoid `%`.\n- The line must not contain `engine/server/api/server.py`, because of the `pgrep -f` matches.\n- The script still detaches and writes `catalog-update-<timestamp>.log`. That file is where the run's outcome and any service-restart failure appear.\n- An overlapping run exits on the lock without touching the pointer.\n- The repo does not install the line.\n- A worktree run shares main's pointer through the `whitelist.db` symlink.\n- Each run calls `run-services.sh stop`/`start` through the shim. That stops and restarts the Client and the translate worker as well as the Engine; an in-flight translation is requeued, with up to 120 s for the worker to stop. The restart runs in cron's minimal environment.\n- The line must set whatever the services need, such as `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<uuid>` before `/usr/bin/bash`. That variable is also inherited by the updater's own GPU stages.\n- A missing `.env.bridge`, `curl` or `ffmpeg` fails the restart unattended.\n- Embeddings and the similarity build now share the GPU with the translate worker daily. A GPU failure there falls back to CPU, which is logged, and the run does not fail.\n\n**Logs:**\n- Add the three new lines: the pointer read (N, stored value, selected group), the group filter (group, kept, removed, channels), and `pointer written last_group=g` / `pointer not advanced: <reason>`.\n- Say that `updater-worker.log` is append-only and unrotated, and now grows daily; suggest a logrotate `copytruncate` rule or periodic truncation.\n- Say that `catalog-update-*.log` files accumulate in the repo root, one per cron run; suggest a pruning line such as `find <repo> -maxdepth 1 -name 'catalog-update-*.log' -mtime +30 -delete`."
    },

Every caller is guarded on N \u2265 1, so `% 0` cannot occur. The host is never re-normalised.\n\n```python\ndef read_increment_pointer(state_path: Path, increments: int) -> tuple[int, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return the group this run crawls and what the pointer file held; refuse a file that cannot be trusted.\"\"\"\n    if not state_path.exists():\n        return 0, \"missing\"\n    fix = f\"fix or delete {state_path} (deleting it restarts at group 0)\"\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(state_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"increment pointer {state_path} is unreadable: {exc}; {fix}\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(state, dict):\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"increment pointer {state_path} is not a JSON object; {fix}\")\n    stored = state.get(\"increments\")\n    last = state.get(\"last_group\")\n    # type() rather than isinstance(): a JSON true/false would otherwise pass as 1/0.\n    if type(stored) is not int or stored < 1:\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"increment pointer {state_path} has increments={stored!r}, not an integer >= 1; {fix}\")\n    if type(last) is not int or not 0 <= last < stored:\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"increment pointer {state_path} has last_group={last!r}, not an integer in [0, {stored}); {fix}\")\n    if stored != increments:\n        return 0, f\"N changed from {stored}, restarting at 0\"\n    return (last + 1) % increments, f\"last_group={last}\"\n```\nHow each case is handled:\n- **Missing key.** `.get` returns `None`, which fails the type check, and the message shows `None`.\n- **Path is a directory.** `read_text` raises `IsADirectoryError`, an `OSError`, so it is refused.\n- **No silent fallback.** There is no broad `except`, so nothing falls back to group 0 silently.\n\n```python\ndef write_increment_pointer(state_path: Path, group: int, increments: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Record `group` as the last completed one: temp file in the same dir, fsync, os.replace.\"\"\"\n    payload = {\n        \"last_group\": group,\n        \"increments\": increments,\n        \"completed_at\": time.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\", time.gmtime()),\n    }\n    tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(\n        mode=\"w\",\n        encoding=\"utf-8\",\n        dir=state_path.parent,\n        prefix=f\"{state_path.stem}.\",\n        suffix=\".tmp\",\n        delete=False,\n    )\n    try:\n        with tmp:\n            json.dump(payload, tmp)\n            tmp.write(\"\\n\")\n            tmp.flush()\n            os.fsync(tmp.fileno())\n        os.replace(tmp.name, state_path)\n    except BaseException:\n        Path(tmp.name).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n        raise\n```\n- **Temp file name.** With the default path the temp file is `updater-increment.<random>.tmp`, which is what `.gitignore` names.\n- **Deliberate simplification: no directory fsync after `os.replace`.**\n  - Ceiling: a power loss right after the replace can bring back the previous pointer, which costs one redundant re-crawl of a group. The INSERT_ONLY merge makes that harmless.\n  - Upgrade path: `os.open(parent, O_RDONLY)` + `os.fsync` + `os.close` after the replace.\n\n```python\ndef filter_staging_to_increment(staging_db: Path, group: int, increments: int) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Delete every staging instance outside `group`, so the crawl stages after it visit only that group's hosts.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(staging_db.as_posix())\n    try:\n        hosts = [row[0] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT host FROM instances WHERE host IS NOT NULL\")]\n        removed = [host for host in hosts if host_increment_group(host, increments) != group]\n        conn.executemany(\"DELETE FROM instances WHERE host = ?\", [(host,) for host in removed])\n        conn.commit()\n        kept = set(hosts) - set(removed)\n        # Counted in Python: an IN (...) over ~1.8k hosts can pass SQLite's host-parameter limit on old builds.\n        channels = sum(\n            int(count)\n            for domain, count in conn.execute(\"SELECT instance_domain, COUNT(*) FROM channels GROUP BY instance_domain\")\n            if domain in kept\n        )\n        logging.info(\n            \"increment filter group=%d hosts_kept=%d hosts_removed=%d staging_channels=%d\",\n            group,\n            len(kept),\n            len(removed),\n            channels,\n        )\n        return {\"kept\": len(kept), \"removed\": len(removed), \"channels\": channels}\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n```\n- **One transaction.** Python's sqlite3 opens an implicit transaction on the first DELETE, and `commit()` closes it.\n- **What it touches.** It writes only to staging `instances`. Seeded `channels` and `videos` rows of other hosts stay put, and prod is never attached.\n- **Empty group.** If the group is empty (tiny dev datasets), the crawl CLIs get an empty host list and the run merges nothing new.   "refactors": "<refactors>\nengine/server/db/jobs/updater-worker.py: in `filter_staging_to_increment`, the kept-host count is now `len(hosts) - len(removed)` (instances.host is the primary key and NULL hosts are already excluded) instead of building a set difference, and the group's staging channels are counted with one `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channels WHERE instance_domain IN (SELECT host FROM instances)` after the delete instead of a Python sum over a GROUP BY. The subquery binds no parameters, so the host-parameter-limit concern and its comment go away. The log line and the returned dict keep the same keys and the same values.\n</refactors>\n\n<left_out>\nReplacing the repeated `args.increments >= 1` guards in `main()` with a local flag or `selected_group is not None`: this saves no lines and the explicit guard reads more plainly. The `os.fdopen` fd leak in `write_increment_pointer` (if fdopen itself raised, the fd would leak): I left it because only a fdopen failure triggers it, and a guard would add code for a case that does not realistically happen. The duplicated `.un/` line in `.gitignore`: it predates this build. The launchers and the fetch-trending comment: nothing in them to simplify. The inner tests the plan lists for the helpers (pointer read edge cases, atomic write, filter counts): no `tests/active` file covers them yet (grep found none), and writing them is new test code rather than a refactor, so it is left for the harvest. The probe `tests/tmp/probe_63_refactor_channel_count.py`, plus the earlier phases' probes in `tests/tmp/probe_63_*`: I have no delete tool, so they need removing by hand. I did not touch any of the gated phase checkpoint files `tests/tmp/test_63_*`.\n</left_out>\n\n<needs_fresh_red>\nnone\n</needs_fresh_red>\n\n<observation>\nI ran a probe on real `schema.sql` staging with 8 hosts, a NULL-host row, a channel on a removed host and an orphan channel.
